title: Notch Filter - Band 30 (2300 MHz) for IoT Narrowband Module
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Elena Vasquez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Notch Filter filter targeting Band 30 (2300 MHz) for IoT Narrowband Module. The filter is designed on Langasite substrate with a target center frequency of 1104.8 MHz and bandwidth of 331.4 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the IoT Narrowband Module module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Notch Filter
- Frequency Band: Band 30 (2300 MHz)
- Application: IoT Narrowband Module
- Substrate: Langasite
- Package: QFN (Quad Flat No-Lead)
- Design Tool: Ansys HFSS 2024R1
- Design Center: San Jose Advanced Design Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the Notch Filter design targeting Band 30 (2300 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       1104.8 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       331.4 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 3.5 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 20.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 43.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 28.0 dB
Q Factor:               5502
Temperature Coefficient:-6.4 ppm/°C
Die Size:               0.9 x 2.3 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   4
Electrode Material:     Al
Passivation:            Si3N4
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Ansys HFSS 2024R1 and load the Notch Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: Langasite with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 1104.8 MHz, BW 331.4 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 3.5 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (QFN (Quad Flat No-Lead)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, Langasite).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz ZNB40.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 3314 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 3.5 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 20.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 497 MHz offset >= 43.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 9 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 0.9 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +31 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 2000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 85%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2025-04-08
Devices Tested:         97
Insertion Loss (meas):  3.2 dB
Return Loss (meas):     21.7 dB
Rejection (meas):       46.0 dB
Isolation (meas):       32.6 dB
Q Factor (meas):        5502
Group Delay Variation:  1.4 ns
Power Handling:         +32 dBm
Die Yield:              94.7%

Result Classification:  CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Notch Filter design demonstrated acceptable performance for Band 30 (2300 MHz).
b) Insertion loss is marginally above target; electrode thickness optimization recommended.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Simulation-to-measurement correlation was within 3% for all key parameters.
e) No delamination observed after 1000-cycle thermal shock test.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
